citation.title: DQN-Based Pre-Optimization for Dual-Scale Collaborative Topology Optimization of Anisotropic Materials
citation.authors: Shuo Feng, Yuhao Yang, Ke Li, Qidong Han, Jinchen Cao, Junyi Du

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Adding DQN pre-optimization to BESO reduced the final MBB beam structural compliance by 22.463% relative to the conventional setting.
claim.location: abstract; numerical values in introduction and Section 5.1/Figure 8
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical and ML runtime pair or numeric speed factor reported.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and conclusion also claim faster convergence qualitatively; Section 5.2 reports a 43.1382% compliance reduction using anisotropic rather than isotropic material, a material comparison.

baseline.classical_method: BESO without DQN pre-optimization/fixed parameter setting (introduction; Section 5.1)
baseline.hardware_ml: PyTorch 2.6.0 CPU version (Section 3.4); processor not stated
baseline.problem_size: 150 x 80 macro elements and 50 x 50 micro elements (Table 4); later MBB generalization 300 x 100 and cantilever 150 x 100 (Section 5.4)
baseline.classical_iterations: not stated for the comparison in Figure 8
baseline.training_time: not stated; DQN updated after each optimization iteration (Section 3.4)
baseline.quality_metric: normalized structural compliance (Section 5.1/Figure 8); volume fraction constraints 0.4 macro, 0.5 micro (Table 4)
baseline.quality_gap: 0.7421 without pre-optimization versus 0.5754 with it, a stated 22.463% reduction (introduction; Section 5.1)

R1.evidence: Abstract: primary quantitative classical comparison is compliance, without a numeric speed comparison.

R2.evidence: Sections 3.4 and 5.1: no comparable hardware, classical solver, or runtimes establish an R2 failure condition.

R3.evidence: Section 3.4: DQN training is concurrent with topology optimization and updated each iteration; no offline training is described for the claim.

R4.evidence: Sections 2 and 5.1/Figure 8: compliance is computed through the method's FE optimization analysis; Table 4 states volume constraints, but achieved volume and failed or infeasible design counts are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: MBB and cantilever beam boundary cases (Section 5.4); eight independent MBB runs (Table 3)

notes: The first quantitative classical comparison in the abstract concerns quality, so the primary stratum is quality despite qualitative convergence claims. Section 3.4 names CPU PyTorch; data availability permits inquiries to the corresponding author.
